title: Preservation Scenarios in DECIDE
summary: When DECIDE writes behavior scenarios for a feature, it also writes preservation scenarios in the same `scenarios.md` block, each asserting an existing observable behavior, contract, or invariant remains unchanged when the feature is exercised, in Given/When/Then form. When the feature genuinely cannot affect existing behavior, the block records a one-line judgment note instead of fabricating a scenario. DECIDE's Step 4 (Behavior Scenarios) is updated to require preservation scenarios for any feature touching existing modules, addressing the DECIDE-phase share of the Einstellung-effect failure chain named in Issue #13.
workflow_point: DECIDE Step 4 (Behavior Scenarios) — preservation scenarios in scenarios.md
mechanism: preservation scenario Given/When/Then block, or a one-line no-existing-behavior judgment note

links.note: gives the Inversion Principle (ADR-055, operationalized as belief-mapping in DISCOVER) a DECIDE-phase scenario-level anchor; preservation scenarios are artifact entries distinct from belief-mapping's conversational question form, and both can fire
preservation scenarios cover criterion-shaped invariants ("X remains unchanged when Y is enabled") at the scenario layer, composing with the Cycle Acceptance Criteria Table (ADR-073)
addresses the DECIDE-phase share of the Issue #13 failure chain; ADR-076 addresses the ARCHITECT-phase share (fitness-criteria decomposition)
